# Meta Said No. That Is Not the End of Your Distribution Plan.

Source: https://lowob.com/research/distribution-when-ad-platforms-restrict-you/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-04-21 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Distribution

> Summary: A rejected ad account is a decision about your category, made by a reviewer who never sees the product. Sort every channel into open, restricted and closed bands for each geography, build first where the answer is already yes, and file restricted-band paperwork with nothing forecast against it. Google, Meta and TikTok all tightened or re-scoped financial and crypto rules in 2025 and 2026, so the map needs a date on it.

A rejected ad account is the first distribution decision made on your behalf, and it is made by a reviewer who never sees the product. Treat the ad platforms as one band of channels among three, not as the plan. Sort every channel into open, restricted or closed for each geography, build first in the open band, and file the restricted-band paperwork with nothing forecast against it. The rules move often: Google added verification for financial advertisers in 24 European markets in June 2026, and Meta made a special ad category mandatory for US financial ads in January 2025.

Somewhere in your company there is a screenshot of a rejected ad account.

It may say the product falls under a restricted financial category. It may ask for a licence number you do not have because your product does not need one. It may say nothing beyond a policy code and a link to an appeal form that leads to another appeal form.

For a large group of legitimate companies, this is the first distribution decision anyone makes on their behalf, and it is made by a reviewer who will never see the product.

The instinct is to treat the rejection as an obstacle to be cleared. Resubmit. Reword. Try a new account. Hire someone who claims to know the trick. That instinct is expensive, and it puts the whole plan at the mercy of a decision the company does not control. The better response is to stop treating the ad platforms as the plan and start treating them as one band of channels among three.

## The rejection is about your category

Platforms publish the rules that produce most rejections, and those rules are written around categories, documents and geographies rather than products. Google's financial products and services policy says advertisers must complete a verification process to advertise financial services in some locations, typically supplying licences and registration numbers. On 23 June 2026 Google announced a new wave covering 24 European Economic Area markets, from Austria to Sweden, with rolling enforcement from 23 July 2026. Advertisers that are not directly authorised by a regulator cannot apply in their own right; an authorised firm must apply for them.

Meta works through targeting rather than only approval. Its developer documentation shows that from January 2025, financial products and services campaigns aimed at US audiences must run in a special ad category, with fixed age ranges, no gender targeting, minimum location radii and no lookalike audiences. A fintech whose plan depended on lookalikes lost that tool on a date it did not choose.

TikTok's financial services policy requires local licensing, disclosures and 18+ targeting for most permitted financial ads, and in many markets crypto advertisers must work with a TikTok sales representative to obtain permission through an application process. None of these steps involve anyone using the product. That is why a rejection says little about whether the product is good, and why rewording rarely changes it. Our explainer on [what a restricted category is](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-restricted-category/) covers how the sorting works.

## Three bands, one honest map

Every channel a company could use sits in one of three bands. The assignment changes by category and geography, so the map is per market, and it carries the date it was checked.

| Band | What it means | Examples (policies checked 16 November 2026) | How to plan |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Carries the category without pre-approval | Affiliate and partner programmes, creator distribution with disclosure, clipping networks, owned email and content, much of programmatic display and video | Build here first and forecast against it |
| Restricted | Carries the category with documentation, licensing or approval | Google financial services verification and crypto certification; Meta's special ad category for US financial ads; TikTok's licensing and permission process for financial and crypto ads | File the paperwork; forecast nothing until it clears |
| Closed | Will not run the category in this geography today, however the copy is worded | Google's global ban on ads for DeFi trading protocols and initial coin offerings; Google's disapproval of binary options; crypto ads in markets where TikTok lists them as not allowed | Write it down as closed and stop proposing it |

Most distribution plans fail because they are written entirely in the restricted band and hope. The company spends its first quarter of budget and attention on getting one platform to say yes, and has nothing built in the band where the answer was already yes.

## Write the closed band down first

This sounds backward. It is the most useful hour in the plan.

List every channel the company would like to use. For each one, record what the platform's published policy says about the category, what documentation it demands, and whether the company can supply it. Where the answer is no, write "closed" and move on. Where the answer is "with paperwork", write down what the paperwork costs in weeks.

| Field | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| Channel and geography | One row per platform per market |
| Policy page and date checked | The platform's own page, with the date you read it |
| Band | Open, restricted or closed |
| Documentation required | Licence, registration number, certification, third-party verifier |
| Can we supply it | Yes, no, or only through a partner's authorisation |
| Weeks to clear | Your honest estimate, with no forecast attached |

Two things happen. The plan stops carrying channels that were never going to work, so forecasts stop being fiction. And the company gains something rare in a sales conversation: the ability to tell a buyer, a board or an investor exactly where it cannot be seen, before anyone else does.

> Ad platforms make one decision about your company. Your distribution plan should never depend on it.

## Build in the open band before asking permission

The open band is not a consolation prize. In categories the platforms review, it is the band where the bidding is thinnest, because the companies that would normally crowd it are still refreshing their appeal status. Our piece on [thin bidding](https://lowob.com/research/thin-bidding/) sets out why the unglamorous channels are often the cheap ones.

A consumer fintech app that cannot get a Meta account approved can still recruit two hundred personal-finance creators on a cost-per-account basis, stand up an affiliate programme on a network that already carries its category, and buy programmatic inventory against audiences it defines itself. None of those channels asked for a licence. All of them report numbers the company can check.

Open does not mean unregulated. The US Federal Trade Commission's guidance for influencers says any financial, employment, personal or family relationship with a brand must be disclosed, placed with the endorsement itself, and in video stated in the video rather than only in the description. Financial regulators apply their own promotion rules on top. The open band is open to the category, not to loose claims. [Partner channel design](https://lowob.com/research/partner-channel-design/) and [referral partners without leakage](https://lowob.com/research/referral-partners-without-leakage/) cover how to structure the terms so the channel holds.

Then, and only then, submit the restricted-band paperwork. If the approval arrives, the company adds a channel to a working system. If it does not, the company has lost a form, not a quarter.

## The plan in four moves

1. **Map the bands truthfully,** in writing, for every geography that matters, using the platforms' own policy pages and dating each entry.
2. **Measure for one week** the two or three open-band channels most likely to carry the product. Small budgets, real tracking, a written question each test must answer. [Campaign testing that reaches a decision](https://lowob.com/research/campaign-testing-that-reaches-a-decision/) covers how to write the decision before the test.
3. **Build the channel that read,** properly: terms, tracking, partner recruitment, creative, reporting.
4. **File restricted-band applications in parallel,** with no forecast attached until they clear.

Re-check the map each quarter. Google posted crypto policy updates in July 2025, September 2025 and February 2026, each opening exchange and wallet advertising in another country under conditions. A channel that was closed last year can become restricted, and a restricted one can tighten.

## What this is not

This is not a method for getting past a platform's review. If a category is closed, it is closed, and a company that pretends otherwise spends money teaching the platform to distrust it.

The platforms say so plainly. Google's circumventing systems policy covers cloaking, creating new accounts after a suspension and supplying false information to verification programmes. It treats violations as egregious: accounts are suspended "upon detection and without prior warning", and the advertiser "will not be allowed to advertise with Google Ads again". Reinstatement happens only in compelling circumstances. A vendor who promises an approval is selling a route to that outcome.

The point is the opposite: know where you cannot be seen, say so, and put the budget where the answer was already yes. Map the three bands, build in the open one, and treat every approval as a bonus rather than a foundation.

## lowob takeaways

- **Read the rejection as a category decision.** It is made from documents and signals, not from the product in use.
- **Map three bands per geography, with dates.** Open, restricted and closed, checked on the platforms' own pages.
- **Build where the answer is already yes.** Affiliate, creators, owned channels and programmatic first.
- **Forecast nothing in the restricted band.** An approval adds a channel; a refusal costs a form.
- **Never circumvent review.** Google bans accounts for it on detection, permanently.
